title: Reconciliation playback simulator for proration migration
creator: Nora Kim
description: Problem: We need to migrate to a new proration canonicalizer (deterministic binning + midcycle allocation policy) but are risk-averse because prior proration tweaks caused invoice noise and customer disputes. Goal: build a deterministic, replayable 'playback simulator' that can run historical raw usage events through the candidate proration/reconciliation logic, surface per-customer delta reports vs current exports, and produce a migration plan with safe canary rollouts and automated rollback triggers. This ticket covers the simulator implementation, dataset pipelines for backfills, diffs generation, and a lightweight web dashboard for reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can run a 90-day historical window (>= 120M events) end-to-end and produce per-account reconciliation diffs within 6 hours
Diff reports include: old_invoice_lines vs new_invoice_lines, net delta in cents, number of altered lines, and root-cause tags (late-webhook, timezone-boundary, plan-swap)
Simulator output is idempotent and signed (canonical hash) so results are reproducible across runs
Provide a canary rollout plan with automated gating: preflight diff < 0.1% of invoices changed for canary orgs, and automated rollback to old export if alert thresholds exceeded
Documentation and a Confluence runbook for finance/ops to review diffs and approve migration
End-to-end unit + integration tests covering DST transitions, out-of-order webhook retries, and midcycle plan swaps
technical_notes: Input sources: raw usage events (ingest ledger), rate-limit credit logs, reserved capacity adjustments, and existing export snapshot files
Canonicalization: normalize timestamps to customer billing timezone using customer.profile.billing_tz; apply deterministic bucket hashing for ties (order by event_id)
Idempotency: compute billing_signature = sha256(customer_id + normalized_ts_bucket + usage_key + plan_id + event_id_fingerprint)
Backfill strategy: run simulator in 'shadow' mode against historical exports and write diffs to GCS 'billing-playback/diffs/YYYY-MM-DD'
Compute infra: Spark job for event join + grouping, then single-node reconciler for invoice-line assembly to keep logic identical to production runtime
Performance: target < 2s per 10k events in reconciler stage; use vectorized proration math and memoized rate lookup
Observability: include per-job checksum, rowcounts, and a sample of top 100 account diffs in job metadata
rollout_plan: 2) Run 90-day shadow playback on 10% sample of customers and review diffs with Finance
3) Address any policy changes identified; iterate on canonicalization rules
4) Canary export: enable new export for 50 low-risk orgs for a 7-day window in parallel with current exports
5) If canary diffs < threshold and no support tickets, gradually expand to 25% of traffic over 2 weeks
6) Full migration and deprecate old exporter after 30 days of stable results
Rollback triggers: >0.25% of invoices with delta > $5 OR any account-level negative-balance anomaly -> auto-disable new exporter and notify finance/ops
monitoring: Dashboard: playback-job success rate, job duration, top 50 accounts by delta, histogram of per-invoice deltas
Alerting: high-delta-rate on canaries, negative-balance regression, checksum mismatch between runs
Audit logs: store canonical run manifest (parameters + data snapshot pointers + checksum) for every playback run
Post-migration: weekly reconciler audit comparing canonicalized exports to NetSuite actuals for first 8 weeks
qa_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization functions with edgecases: DST switches, leap seconds, sub-minute events
Integration test: full run on synthetic dataset with injected late retries and duplicate webhooks, assert idempotency
Manual review: finance team sign-off on representative diffs for top 500 revenue accounts
Post-canary smoke tests: verify NetSuite line totals for canary orgs reconcile to new export within tolerance
